title: Four-layer stackup selection and review workflow
summary: Review layer roles together with fabrication and circuit requirements. Compare alternatives using the linked guides before selecting a construction.
applies_to: Planning a four-layer board; workflow is an editorial synthesis.
required_inputs: Device and interface requirements; power rails; mechanical constraints; fabricator capabilities
verification: Record the selected construction and inspect routing, power integrity and product EMC evidence.
limitations: No stackup guarantees compliance. Retrieved guidance does not select CAD constraints automatically.

title: Four-layer option with two inner ground references
summary: Consider L1 signal/power, L2 GND, L3 GND, L4 signal/power when both outer routing layers need adjacent ground. Budget surface power distribution explicitly.
applies_to: Nonisolated layouts where surface routing can accommodate power.
verification: Inspect both outer routes and their ground references.
limitations: This option trades a dedicated power plane for ground referencing; it is not mandatory for every design.

citations.locator: Determining Layer Count and Stack-Up, numbered option 1; For a 4-Layer Board

title: Four-layer option with an inner power plane
summary: L1 signal, L2 GND, L3 power, L4 signal is an NXP example. Review the actual reference of L4 routes, especially where L3 contains separate rails.
applies_to: Four-layer designs considering a dedicated power layer.
required_inputs: Power islands and critical bottom routes
verification: Map each bottom route to its adjacent copper.
limitations: The MCXA example is device-scoped; it does not make every bottom-layer route acceptable.

title: Review the fabrication and rework cost of outer ground layers
summary: An alternative uses outer ground layers with inner signal/power routing. Assess component access and via transitions before choosing this arrangement.
applies_to: Designs evaluating buried routing between outer ground layers.
verification: Review access to buried connections and reference continuity.
limitations: NXP notes difficult rework. Surface pads and openings mean the outer copper is not a complete enclosure.

title: Specify dielectric gaps rather than only total board thickness
summary: For outer signals and inner planes, review thin outer dielectric gaps and a thicker center core. Total board thickness alone does not specify signal-to-reference spacing.
applies_to: Four-layer constructions with outer signal layers.
verification: Check each signal-to-plane gap in the approved build.
limitations: A thicker center reduces inner-plane coupling; do not assume all adjacent copper layers are tightly coupled.

title: Review fast signals adjacent to power copper
summary: Prefer a continuous ground reference for fast interfaces. If power referencing is unavoidable, review the AC return connection between power and ground; a ground via alone cannot join different reference nets.
applies_to: High-speed signal conditioners and USB hubs; apply exact device requirements.
verification: Inspect the return circuit, including its capacitor connections.
limitations: Return-path capacitors are not series data-line coupling capacitors. Do not bridge isolation barriers using this guidance.

title: Evaluate inner-plane capacitance and discrete decoupling together
summary: Closely spaced power and ground planes improve high-frequency coupling. Check their actual separation and overlap before relying on this effect.
required_inputs: Dielectric construction and rail transient requirements
verification: Review the supply impedance and local bypass connections.
limitations: Four layers do not justify removing device-required decoupling capacitors.

title: Keep vendor stackup examples and EMC heuristics conditional
summary: Treat NXP construction dimensions and the 20-H edge-setback suggestion as contextual guidance, not universal manufacturing limits or compliance evidence.
applies_to: Transferring application-note recommendations to another product.
required_inputs: Source device scope and product requirements
verification: Record which assumptions transfer and which need verification.
limitations: A layer-count label or heuristic cannot certify an assembled product.

title: Reconsider four layers when routing requirements cannot be met
summary: Consider more layers when required routing structures and reference continuity cannot fit the four-layer construction.
applies_to: Dense or demanding designs evaluating a four-layer limit.
verification: Review the most constrained paths before fixing layer count.
limitations: A vendor comparison table is not a prediction that every four-layer board fails EMC.
